clue.text: Scholar there in France has support from Lydia's aunt

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree
la is French for 'there'
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: A French-speaking academic is propped up by a relative of someone called Lydia.
explanation.walkthrough: Lydia Languish is the heroine of Sheridan's play The Rivals; her aunt is the word-mangling Mrs Malaprop.
explanation.definitionFit: In Sheridan's comedy The Rivals the heroine Lydia Languish is chaperoned by her aunt, Mrs Malaprop.

clue.text: Very strict chap with the heart of 29

parts.note: Martin is a man's name, standing for any chap

indicators.note: takes the central letters of the word supplied by clue 29

parts.note: refers to the answer at 29 across, the African fly

explanation.surface: A stern fellow who goes to the centre of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a noun for a stern disciplinarian; 'Very strict' stands for it as a description of such a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a rigid disciplinarian, named after a severe French army drillmaster.

clue.text: Binders to suit Elgar's variation

indicators.note: a variation alters the theme, so these letters are rearranged; a nod to Elgar's Enigma Variations

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Ties chosen to match a composer's set of variations.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that bind or tie, such as cords or surgical threads.

clue.text: Cherubic figures set it up

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Angel statues are arranged for display.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump naked infant angels in Renaissance art are known by this Italian plural.

clue.text: So retrograde to be so large

definitions.text: So retrograde to be so large

parts.words: So retrograde to be so large
parts.note: read backwards the word so gives OS, the clothing label meaning extra large

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something going backwards to grow so big.
explanation.walkthrough: OS, seen on clothing labels, abbreviates the answer; reverse SO and you have it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments marked OS are of a size larger than standard.

clue.text: Marvellous West Pyrenean goat-antelope

parts.note: the izard is the chamois of the Pyrenees, a goat-antelope

explanation.surface: Admiring a fine mountain animal seen in the western Pyrenees.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an exclamation or adjective, it is informal praise meaning excellent or brilliant.

clue.text: Lived in it behind a redevelopment

indicators.note: a building's redevelopment rebuilds it, so these letters are reconstructed in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone occupied a home at the back of a building site.
explanation.definitionFit: A house that is lived in has residents occupying it.

clue.text: Some trouble on foot, with a bit of the mast

parts.note: a corn is a painful patch of hard skin on the foot

explanation.surface: A sailor with foot trouble climbs part of the ship's mast.
explanation.walkthrough: Mast here is not a ship's pole but the fallen nuts of forest trees, eaten by pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the fallen fruit of oak and beech; an oak's nut is one piece of it.

clue.text: .Assimilate a code of laws

definitions.meaning: to absorb mentally or take in
a compilation of laws, like Justinian's

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to take in or absorb; as a noun it is a systematic summary of legal rules.

clue.text: Is a bang on the head such a benefit?

definitions.text: Is a bang on the head such a benefit?

parts.words: Is a bang on the head such a benefit?
parts.note: bangs is the American word for hair cut straight across the forehead, and a perk on top of pay is a benefit of the same name

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a knock to the skull could do you good.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair cut across the forehead and an extra perk beyond salary share this name.

clue.text: Just instruct the amanuensis orally

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the phrase before it is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: an amanuensis is a secretary taking dictation, so you tell them to write

explanation.surface: Someone merely gives spoken orders to a secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' in the surface, but it is the definition in its sense of fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and correct, a sense shared with right.

clue.text: Number symbolizing the flame of unrequited love?

definitions.text: Number symbolizing the flame of unrequited love?

parts.words: Number symbolizing the flame of unrequited love?
parts.note: a number is a song, and someone pining for a lost love is said to carry a flame for them

explanation.surface: Asking which song best represents hopeless longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentimental ballad of unreturned love takes its name from carrying a torch for someone.

clue.text: Instinctive apprehension in teaching

parts.note: tuition is teaching or instruction

explanation.surface: Gut feeling plays its part in education.
explanation.definitionFit: It is understanding gained by instinct rather than by reasoning.

clue.text: Business head has obligation to make an extra payment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so take the start of the word business

parts.note: an onus is a burden or obligation

explanation.surface: A company boss is bound to hand out additional pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid on top of normal wages is a bonus.

clue.text: Definition of nostalgia after loss of directions

definitions.text: Definition of nostalgia after loss of directions

parts.words: Definition of nostalgia after loss of directions
parts.note: removing the compass points N and S from the word nostalgia leaves otalgia, the medical term for pain in the ear

explanation.surface: Looking up homesickness in a dictionary after losing one's way.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are the directions; take them out of nostalgia and the medical word otalgia remains, which is defined by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical name for pain felt in the ear.

clue.text: Old-fashioned gimlet for instance

parts.note: an old-fashioned and a gimlet are both mixed drinks, not an antique boring tool

explanation.surface: An antique hand drill offered as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mixed drinks: whiskey with bitters, and gin with lime cordial.

clue.text: Be not distressed about first of many put in the vault

indicators.note: placed around, so the shuffled letters go about the next piece
upset or troubled, so the letters of be not are disturbed into a new order
picks just the opening letter of the word many

explanation.surface: Don't be upset that most people end up buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' turns BE NOT into ENTOB; 'about' puts the M from 'first of many' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To place a body in a tomb or burial vault.

clue.text: Watch new-style In The Mood, by The Splinters

indicators.note: placed inside, so the shuffled letters go in the word mood
given a new style, so the letters of watch are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Glenn Miller swing hit reworked by a band called The Splinters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new-style' rearranges WATCH as ATCHW, which 'In' puts inside MOOD. In The Mood is a famous 1939 big-band tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood reduced to tiny fragments, as in 'smashed to matchwood', is splinters.

clue.text: One will seize its quarry or depart in confusion

indicators.note: jumbled and disordered, so the letters of or depart are mixed up

explanation.surface: An animal either grabs its prey or flees in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting animal catches prey for food.

clue.text: Cupid's sole love — so we hear

definitions.text: Cupid's sole love — so we hear

parts.words: Cupid's sole love — so we hear
parts.note: in myth Cupid loved only the princess ..., and the Greek word for soul sounds like 'sole'

explanation.surface: A rumour that the god of love was faithful to just one woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: Cupid's beloved in myth, and the soul (sounding like 'sole'), since the Greek name means soul.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth the mortal princess loved by Cupid bears this name, which is also Greek for the soul or spirit.

clue.text: By no means genuine holding of bankers at Zurich

indicators.note: the words that follow hold the answer within them, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Swiss banks hold investments that are fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Substitute or imitation, as of a poor replacement for the real thing.

clue.text: He looks at books for The Listener

definitions.meaning: someone who inspects a company's accounts
one who hears, from Latin audire, to hear

explanation.definitionFit: An accountant who checks financial records is one, and the Latin root means a hearer, as in the audience.

clue.text: Time in which river flowed to order

indicators.note: the time word holds the others inside it

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
ran means flowed, as water does

explanation.surface: An era when a river was made to run as instructed.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things in order or sequence is to arrange them.

clue.text: Set up big stake as gallows

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is written upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a bet is a stake wagered

explanation.surface: Erecting a large post to hang people from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stake' suggests a post, but it is a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright post with an arm from which executed criminals were hung.

clue.text: Sounds a small opening — an inch in Scotland

indicators.note: signals that the phrase after it is heard as a word spelt differently

parts.note: an eyelet is a small hole for a lace or cord

explanation.surface: A tiny gap described in Scottish units of length.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland an inch is a small island (Inchcolm, Inchkeith), not the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch is the Scots word for a small island, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Account book detailed for the shelf

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts

explanation.surface: Finance records itemised and placed on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow projecting surface like a mantel or rock shelf.

clue.text: Scored but withdrew from contest

definitions.meaning: marked with a cut or line
pulled out of a race before the start, as a horse may be

explanation.definitionFit: It means both marked with a sharp point and taken out of a race or competition.

clue.text: Robots put in to find a city

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's play that introduced the word robot

explanation.surface: Automatons are installed to locate an urban centre.
explanation.walkthrough: TRURO is the cathedral city of Cornwall, England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the county city of Cornwall, with a cathedral.

clue.text: Where sportsmen in Gloucestershire made the feathers fly

definitions.text: Where sportsmen in Gloucestershire made the feathers fly

parts.words: Where sportsmen in Gloucestershire made the feathers fly
parts.note: the shuttlecock game is named after the Duke of Beaufort's house in Gloucestershire, an English county, where it was played

explanation.surface: Describing a country estate where hunters scattered game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feathers fly' suggests shooting birds; it is the feathered shuttlecock. The game took its name from a ducal estate in Gloucestershire, a county in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: The racket game with a shuttlecock is named after the stately home where it was popularised.

clue.text: Destroyer about to destroy this?

parts.note: a destroyer is a fast warship whose wartime task was hunting enemy submarines

explanation.surface: A wrecker on the point of wrecking something.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine was the prime target of a destroyer's depth charges.

clue.text: Fly repeatedly back east across the Channel

read in reverse, the word for east is turned round

parts.note: est is French for east, France being across the Channel

explanation.surface: An insect keeps returning to France.

clue.text: Judicial type of instrument

definitions.meaning: a part-time judge in England and Wales
a woodwind instrument played by blowing

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a barrister sitting as a part-time judge in Britain and a simple wooden flute.
